Changing the date adds no coverage.

panel.summary: `touchUpdatedAt`'s monotonic guard (`where: { updatedAt: { lt: at } }`) is untested — the idempotency/out-of-order property the code and webhook rely on is unverified
panel.evidence: document.service.ts adds `touchUpdatedAt` whose whole point (per its docstring) is that it only moves time forward and no-ops on missing rows. document.service.spec.ts (new in this diff) tests only `updateDocument`; it never constructs a service with an `updateMany` mock. The controller spec mocks `touchUpdatedAt` away entirely (yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts:9-12), so no test would catch dropping the `lt` filter and letting an out-of-order/duplicate webhook move `updatedAt` backwards.

coderabbit.summary: Use a past date in the `issuedAt` test to avoid time-dependent failures.
coderabbit.detail: **Use a past date in the `issuedAt` test to avoid time-dependent failures.** The test expects `touchUpdatedAt` to be called with `new Date('2026-07-10T06:03:13.331Z')`, but the controller clamps `issuedAt` to `now()` via `Math.min(issuedMs, now)`. If the test executes before that exact UTC moment, the clamp kicks in and `touchUpdatedAt` receives `now()` instead — causing a flaky failure. Using a clearly historical date eliminates this fragility.
coderabbit.finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts::use a past date in the `issuedat` test to avoid time-dependent failures.
